en: The Sūtra on the Lightness and Heaviness of the Retribution for Violating the Precepts Spoken by the Buddha.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Rājagṛha in the Kalandaka Bamboo Grove.
At that time, the Venerable Maudgalyāyana arose from meditation in the late afternoon and went to where the World-Honored One was, prostrating his head [at the Buddha’s feet].
Having prostrated at his feet, he withdrew and sat to one side.
Then the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
"I have a doubt and now wish to question you;
I only pray that you will grant me permission.
The Buddha told Maudgalyāyana:
"I shall listen to your question and explain it for you.
Maudgalyāyana then addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"

If a bhikṣu or bhikṣuṇī, lacking a sense of shame and remorse, treats the Buddha’s teachings with contempt and violates the rules of training (śaikṣa-dharma), and likewise commits offenses such as pāyattika, pāṭidesanīya, sthūlātyaya, saṃghāvaśeṣa, or pārājika, how many unwholesome transgressions does he or she incur?
“I only pray that you will explain it.
The Buddha told Maudgalyāyana:
“Listen attentively; I shall explain it for you.”
If a bhikṣu or bhikṣuṇī, being shameless and lacking a sense of propriety, treats the Buddha’s words with contempt and violates the rules of training (śaikṣa-dharma),
they will fall into hell for a lifespan equal to five hundred years as reckoned by the Four Great Kings, which corresponds to nine hundred thousand years by human calculation.
The Buddha told Maudgalyāyana:
"If one lacks a sense of shame and remorse, treats the Buddha’s words with contempt, and commits an offense of *pātideśanīya*,
they shall fall into hell for a lifespan equal to one thousand years in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, which, by human reckoning, is three hundred and sixty million years."
The Buddha said to Maudgalyāyana:
"If one lacks a sense of shame and remorse, treats the Buddha’s words with contempt, and commits an offense, it constitutes a *pāyattika*.
Such a person will fall into hell for a lifespan of two thousand years as measured by the Yāma Heaven, which corresponds to twenty-four billion years by human reckoning."
The Buddha told Maudgalyāyana:
"If one lacks shame and remorse, treats the Buddha’s words with contempt, and commits this offense, it constitutes a sthūlātyaya.
As for the lifespan of four thousand years in the Tuṣita Heaven, when measured by human reckoning, it is fifty billion and sixty thousand years in the hells."
The Buddha told Maudgalyāyana:
"If one lacks a sense of shame and remorse, treats the Buddha’s words with contempt, and commits an offense against the Saṃghāvaśeṣa, it is as follows:
just as a deva of the Nirmāṇarati heaven who lives for eight thousand years falls into hell, that duration corresponds to two hundred and forty billion times ten million years by human reckoning."
The Buddha told Maudgalyāyana:
"If one lacks shame and remorse, treats the Buddha’s words with contempt, and commits a *pārājika* offense,

they will fall into hell for a lifespan equal to sixteen thousand years as reckoned by the Paranirmita-vaśavartin gods— nine hundred twenty-one billion and ninety thousand years by human calculation."
At that time, the Venerable Maudgalyāyana, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
Then Maudgalyāyana spoke these verses:
"Because of the cause and condition of contempt, One’s life-force leads to falling into the evil realms."
By practicing virtue through causes and conditions, one is reborn in the heavens in this life.
By cultivating wholesome karma on this basis, one leaves evil behind and attains liberation;
yet by failing to contemplate causes and conditions, one enters the evil realms when the body perishes.
” Thus it was said.
